pr_title: Make Sonos alarm `unique_id` unique with multiple households
pr_body:
<!--

## Breaking change
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
In very specific scenarios where a user is running multiple Sonos systems (households) and where alarm_id values happen to conflict, the `unique_id` are not unique enough. This PR adds use of the household ID to ensure the `unique_id` is actually unique in these setups.

A migration is also performed for "old" `unique_id` values which should work for ~99% of installations. If an installation uses multiple Sonos households _and_ has an alarm ID duplication, the migration will process the first alarm it sees. This has a possibility of migrating the incorrect alarm, but there is currently not enough information stored to guarantee this step. Either way, this will allow those setups to register entities for both alarms which was not possible previously.

issue_context.title: Sonos: Platform sonos does not generate unique IDs
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have two separate Sonos environments (different Sonos accounts) on the same network. When the switch.sonos_alarm_XXX entities are getting populated (f.e. after installing or reinstalling the integration)
, the homeassistant sonos integration tries to creates the same uniqueID for different alarms.
This leads to one alarm being not available in homeassistant (see logs below).

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.12.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Sonos

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sonos/

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.switch] Platform sonos does not generate unique IDs. ID sonos-4 is already used by switch.sonos_alarm_4 - ignoring switch.sonos_alarm_4
```


### Additional information

The sonos integration configuration was done via the UI without any additional configuration entries in the configuration.yaml.
Deleting the integration > Restart HA > Installing the integration = Does not resolve the issue.

review_comments: Is there a way we can tell if they have already been migrated and return early without iterating them all?
I suppose we could do something like bump the config entry version, but I'm not sure that would be best practice.
Config entry version number is a good idea
Per discussion in discord, since this only happens when they are added (not always) and its only temporary, it not going to be a problem to let it check every time.
Is there a better way than checking the icon?

That has been the default icon since the feature was added. This seemed easier than parsing the `entity_id` or `original_name` strings. (It's also why the new `unique_id` has "alarm" in the string.)

For reference, here's what's available in the entity registry for "old" alarms:
```json
            {
                "area_id": null,
                "capabilities": null,
                "config_entry_id": "c9145e60ca0bf47a27e168debc5b5854",
                "device_class": null,
                "device_id": "d6931d510a72b2ff5db5de54a7d021b8",
                "disabled_by": null,
                "entity_category": "config",
                "entity_id": "switch.sonos_alarm_7831",
                "icon": null,
                "id": "f6010779b6269e23884cf0116f4b5dfb",
                "name": null,
                "original_device_class": null,
                "original_icon": "mdi:alarm",
                "original_name": "Bedroom Daily Alarm 07:00",
                "platform": "sonos",
                "supported_features": 0,
                "unique_id": "sonos-7831",
                "unit_of_measurement": null
            }
```
Its a bit ugly, but it should be deterministic in this case
